note: Synthetic reports written for this project. No patient data, no PHI, safe to keep in a public repository. These are a smoke test, not a validation set: they check that the extractor's failure modes behave, not that it performs well. Real metrics require a labelled corpus under LABELLING.md.

cases.why: C2. Most reports look like this. A model that dislikes empty output will invent something here, and that is the failure mode that makes the system net-harmful.
cases.report:
EXAMINATION: CHEST X-RAY PA AND LATERAL
DATE OF STUDY: 2026-03-14

COMPARISON: None available.

FINDINGS: The lungs are clear. No focal consolidation, pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits. Osseous structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: Normal chest radiograph.

cases.why: The straightforward case. Should extract one recommendation with a 6 month interval and a valid span.
cases.report:
EXAMINATION: CT CHEST WITHOUT CONTRAST
DATE OF STUDY: 2026-03-14

FINDINGS: There is an 8 mm solid nodule in the right upper lobe. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. No pleural effusion.

IMPRESSION: 8 mm right upper lobe pulmonary nodule. Recommend CT follow-up in 6 months.

cases.why: Rule 3 and R6. The model knows Fleischner intervals and will want to supply one. It must return interval null. A guideline default applied here would be an unattributable due date.
cases.report:
EXAMINATION: CT CHEST
DATE OF STUDY: 2026-02-02

IMPRESSION: 5 mm solid nodule in the left lower lobe. Follow-up as per Fleischner criteria.

expect.comment: interval MUST be null. Any populated interval here is a rule 3 violation and should also be caught by the interval_verbatim check.

cases.why: C1 boundary and the hardest case. A significant finding is described and nothing is recommended. Clinically a reader wants to act; the extractor must not. This is the single most likely place for the system to invent an obligation.
cases.report:
EXAMINATION: CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST
DATE OF STUDY: 2026-01-20

FINDINGS: A 2.1 cm hypodense lesion is noted in the right hepatic lobe, unchanged in size and appearance from the prior study of 2024. Kidneys, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: Stable 2.1 cm right hepatic lesion, unchanged since 2024.

cases.why: Conditional follow-up must be flagged, not converted into an unconditional due date.
cases.report:
EXAMINATION: ULTRASOUND ABDOMEN
DATE OF STUDY: 2026-04-05

IMPRESSION: No acute abnormality identified. Consider repeat ultrasound in 3 months if symptoms persist.

cases.why: An explicit statement that follow-up is not required is evidence, not absence. It supports the not_indicated terminal state and must be captured rather than discarded.
cases.report:
EXAMINATION: CT CHEST
DATE OF STUDY: 2026-05-11

IMPRESSION: 3 mm subpleural nodule, benign appearance. No further imaging follow-up is required.

cases.why: Two distinct recommended actions in one report must produce two instances, not one merged instance.
cases.report:
EXAMINATION: CT CHEST WITH CONTRAST
DATE OF STUDY: 2026-06-18

IMPRESSION: 1.4 cm right upper lobe mass, suspicious. Recommend PET-CT and referral to the respiratory multidisciplinary team.

expect.comment: One imaging action and one referral action.

cases.why: Follow-up already arranged must not generate a duplicate obligation.
cases.report:
EXAMINATION: CT ABDOMEN
DATE OF STUDY: 2026-06-30

IMPRESSION: 1.8 cm left adrenal nodule with indeterminate features. The patient is already booked for adrenal protocol MRI next month.

cases.why: A report with no date must yield date_found null, never today's date. Every due date is derived from this field, so a silently substituted date produces a silently wrong obligation.
cases.report: IMPRESSION: 7 mm nodule in the left upper lobe. Recommend interval CT in 12 months.

cases.why: Generic closing boilerplate naming no specific test is not a recommendation. Treating it as one would generate obligations on a large share of all reports.
